_comment: Wrong-fact probes for evals/scripts/run_lift.py --probes. Each probe is a claim corrected on 2026-10-19 in the R1-07 / R1-08 batch-1 skills (the wrong_answer is the pre-fix text, close to verbatim; correct_answer is the fixed claim). source = Summer '26 corpus file + line.

probes.question: I'm writing a client that downloads the results of a Bulk API 2.0 query job set by set. How does the client know it has fetched the last set of results?
probes.wrong_answer: The Sforce-Locator response header is only present while more pages exist; when it is absent or empty on a response, that was the last page.
probes.correct_answer: On the last set the Sforce-Locator header is still returned but its value is the literal string 'null'; keep requesting with the locator until the header's value is the string 'null'.

probes.question: My CSV for a Bulk API 2.0 ingest job is 400 MB raw. Can I just PUT it to the same job in 100 MB pieces to stay under the upload limit?
probes.wrong_answer: Yes. The 150 MB (base64) limit applies to each PUT request, so repeat the PUT for every chunk on the same job before closing it.
probes.correct_answer: No. The roughly 150 MB base64 (about 100 MB raw) limit covers the data of the whole job, so a 400 MB file has to be split across several jobs.

probes.question: I'm doing a Bulk API 2.0 update from a CSV in which some cells are empty because the source value is blank. Will those Salesforce fields be cleared?
probes.wrong_answer: An empty cell sets the field to an empty string/null on update, so blank cells clear the field; use #N/A only for fields that must be a true null.
probes.correct_answer: No. Empty field values are ignored when you update records; to set a field to null the cell must contain #N/A.

probes.question: How do I turn on PK chunking for a Bulk API 2.0 query job over 40 million Account rows?
probes.wrong_answer: You can't: PK chunking only exists in Bulk API v1 (Sforce-Enable-PKChunking header), so use v1 for that export.
probes.correct_answer: Bulk API 2.0 query jobs perform PK chunking automatically, so there is nothing to enable (the manually invoked Sforce-Enable-PKChunking header is the Bulk API v1 mechanism).

probes.question: A Bulk API 2.0 ingest job ended in state JobComplete. Which result sets must I read to account for every uploaded row?
probes.wrong_answer: All three, always: successfulResults, failedResults and unprocessedRecords, and the three counts must add up to the rows uploaded.
probes.correct_answer: successfulResults and failedResults account for the rows of a JobComplete job; the unprocessedrecords resource exists only for failed or aborted jobs.

probes.question: Our Opportunity table has 10 million rows and the filter field has a custom index. Roughly how many rows can my filter match before the optimizer stops using that custom index?
probes.wrong_answer: About 333,333 rows: the custom-index threshold is capped at 333,333 targeted records no matter how large the table is.
probes.correct_answer: There is no flat cap: a custom index is used if the filter matches less than 10% of the first million rows plus less than 5% of the rest, which is about 550,000 rows for a 10-million-row table.

probes.question: Support created a custom index on production for us. Will that index exist in our Partial and Developer sandboxes, so I can check query plans there?
probes.wrong_answer: No. Custom indexes created in production are copied to Full sandboxes only; Developer, Developer Pro and Partial sandboxes do not receive them.
probes.correct_answer: Yes. Custom indexes that Salesforce Customer Support creates in production are copied to all sandboxes created from that production org (skinny tables are the ones copied to Full sandboxes only).

probes.question: A SOQL query on a 5M-row object filters on a non-deterministic formula field AND on an indexed field that matches under 1% of the rows. Is the query doomed to a full table scan because of the formula field?
probes.wrong_answer: Yes. A WHERE filter on a non-deterministic formula field can never be indexed, so the query will always be a full-table scan whatever else is in the WHERE clause.
probes.correct_answer: No. The formula field cannot be indexed, but only that filter is excluded; another indexed filter in the WHERE clause that meets the selectivity thresholds can still drive the query.

probes.question: Our Case table has 2 million rows and we are asking Support for a custom index. Is 'the filter returns no more than 200,000 records' a safe rule for the optimizer to use it?
probes.wrong_answer: Yes. Keeping the filter at or under about 200,000 records is the recommended target for large orgs, whatever the table size.
probes.correct_answer: No. There is no flat row target: the custom-index threshold scales with the table, 10% of the first million plus 5% of the rest, which is 150,000 rows for a 2-million-row table, so a filter matching 200,000 rows would not use the index.

probes.question: I filter on a custom picklist field all the time and want it indexed. Can I get an index simply by ticking External ID on that picklist?
probes.wrong_answer: Yes. External ID can be set on any custom field and automatically creates an index on it.
probes.correct_answer: No. External ID can be created only on Auto Number, Email, Number and Text fields; an index on other field types, or on standard fields, has to be requested from Salesforce Customer Support.

probes.question: From Apex saved at API 60.0 I insert an Account whose custom Text(255) field is given a 300-character string. What happens?
probes.wrong_answer: Salesforce silently truncates the value to 255 characters and the insert succeeds.
probes.correct_answer: The insert fails with an error because the value is too large; only if allowFieldTruncation is set does Apex truncate it instead.

probes.question: We are loading 80 million rows into an empty custom object for the first time. For raw load speed, should the job be insert or upsert?
probes.wrong_answer: Always upsert with an External ID, even for the first load; there is no speed penalty and re-runs are then always safe.
probes.correct_answer: insert() is the fastest operation, then update(), then upsert(), so for a very large first load into an empty object an insert pass is the faster choice (switch to upsert for re-runs).

probes.question: Our nightly purge batch deletes 500,000 records and we fear a storage alert. Should finish() call Database.emptyRecycleBin() to give the storage back?
probes.wrong_answer: Yes. Soft-deleted records stay in the Recycle Bin for up to 15 days and keep counting against data storage, so emptying the bin reclaims the storage immediately.
probes.correct_answer: Not for storage: items in the Recycle Bin don't count against the org's storage. Emptying it only makes the rows unrecoverable and removes soft-deleted rows that still burden queries.

probes.question: Our org just hit its data storage limit and inserts are blocked. Is emptying the Recycle Bin the fastest way to free space?
probes.wrong_answer: Yes. Empty the Recycle Bin first: deleted records stay there for up to 15 days and still count against data storage, so this is the fastest win.
probes.correct_answer: No. Items in the Recycle Bin don't count against storage, so emptying it won't free any; you need to remove or archive real records.

probes.question: Which values can AuthorizationFormConsent.Status hold, and how should I record a patient who declines the authorization?
probes.wrong_answer: Only Seen and Signed; a decline is modelled by not creating the consent row or by deleting it.
probes.correct_answer: Status is a restricted picklist with three values, Rejected, Seen and Signed; a patient who declines is recorded with Status = Rejected.

probes.question: What values are valid for ConsentCapturedSourceType when a patient gives consent by phone or by postal mail?
probes.wrong_answer: The source type picklist is Web, Email, Verbal or Paper, so use Verbal for phone and Paper for mail.
probes.correct_answer: It is a restricted picklist with Email, InPerson, MailingAddress, Phone, Social, Video and Web, so use Phone or MailingAddress.

probes.question: On AuthorizationFormConsent, can ConsentGiverId point at a Contact, or must it be an Individual Id?
probes.wrong_answer: It must be an Individual Id; a Contact, Account or person-account Id is not valid there.
probes.correct_answer: ConsentGiverId is a polymorphic lookup that accepts Account, Contact, Individual, Lead or User, so a Contact Id is valid.

probes.question: Which two objects does an AuthorizationFormDataUse row link, so I can tell which purposes a consent form covers?
probes.wrong_answer: It links an AuthorizationFormText (the form version) to a DataUsePurpose, so each new text version needs its own data-use rows.
probes.correct_answer: It links an AuthorizationForm to a DataUsePurpose (AuthorizationFormId and DataUsePurposeId), so purposes attach to the form, not to a text version.

probes.question: In a .matchingRule metadata file, which matchingMethod value do I use to fuzzy-match company names?
probes.wrong_answer: FuzzyCompanyName.
probes.correct_answer: CompanyName; the valid matchingMethod values are Exact, FirstName, LastName, CompanyName, Phone, City, Street, Zip and Title.

probes.question: Which matchingMethod can I put on a matching-rule item to match email addresses?
probes.wrong_answer: Email is one of the matching methods (alongside Exact, Phone and the fuzzy methods).
probes.correct_answer: There is no Email matching method; the valid values are Exact, FirstName, LastName, CompanyName, Phone, City, Street, Zip and Title, so email is matched with Exact.

probes.question: I need two separate Account matching rules, one for B2B and one for B2C, in source format. What does the metadata look like?
probes.wrong_answer: One MatchingRule element per rule, each declared with fullName="Account.<RuleName>" as its own element.
probes.correct_answer: One file, matchingRules/Account.matchingRule, with a MatchingRules root that holds one <matchingRules> child (with its own <fullName>) per rule.

probes.question: Can I delete a custom object's Record Type with a destructiveChanges.xml deployment, or is that impossible through the Metadata API?
probes.wrong_answer: Impossible: Record Types cannot be deleted via the Metadata API, so they must be removed manually in Setup.
probes.correct_answer: The RecordType metadata type is documented to create, update or delete record type definitions for a custom object, so it can be listed in a destructive manifest (an in-use record type may still fail, so reassign it first).

probes.question: I must delete Apex class Foo and add a replacement Foo in the same deployment. With a plain destructiveChanges.xml, when does the delete run relative to the additions in package.xml?
probes.wrong_answer: After the additions; to delete first you must use destructiveChangesPre.xml.
probes.correct_answer: By default deletions are processed before additions, so a plain destructiveChanges.xml already deletes first; destructiveChangesPost.xml is the variant that deletes after the additions.

probes.question: What is the SiteDotCom folder called in my SFDX project, so I can put it in .forceignore?
probes.wrong_answer: siteDotCom/ (so the ignore rule is **/siteDotCom/**).
probes.correct_answer: SiteDotCom components are stored in the siteDotComSites directory, so the ignore rule is **/siteDotComSites/**.

probes.question: Is SiteDotCom a metadata type that can never be deployed, so I should drop it from every manifest permanently?
probes.wrong_answer: Yes. SiteDotCom is never deployable; it is a platform-generated blob that should be excluded from every manifest.
probes.correct_answer: No. SiteDotCom is a deployable metadata type in its own right (API 30.0 and later); the rule is that it must not be in the manifest of a deployment that carries the site's ExperienceBundle.

probes.question: Which code coverage rule applies to a deployment run with RunLocalTests versus one run with RunSpecifiedTests?
probes.wrong_answer: The same for both: overall org coverage must be at least 75% and every deployed class must also reach 75% individually.
probes.correct_answer: With all or all-local tests overall coverage must be at least 75% (triggers need some coverage); with RunSpecifiedTests each class and trigger being deployed must be covered at least 75% individually.

probes.question: How do I switch on 'Enable ExperienceBundle Metadata API' in every new scratch org without clicking through Setup?
probes.wrong_answer: You can't: the checkbox cannot be set through the scratch org definition or metadata, so a manual Setup step is needed in each org.
probes.correct_answer: It is ordinary settings metadata: deploy ExperienceBundle settings (settings/ExperienceBundle.settings with enableExperienceBundleMetadata set to true) as a post-create step; the field defaults to false.

probes.question: My LWR site was created before Winter '23 and is not an enhanced LWR site. Which metadata type do I retrieve, ExperienceBundle or DigitalExperienceBundle?
probes.wrong_answer: DigitalExperienceBundle: all LWR sites use it, and ExperienceBundle returns an empty retrieve for an LWR site.
probes.correct_answer: DigitalExperienceBundle is only for enhanced LWR sites created in Winter '23 or later; Aura sites and other LWR sites use ExperienceBundle.

probes.question: Can a post-deploy script read a Named Credential's endpoint with SOQL, or are named credentials not queryable?
probes.wrong_answer: They cannot be queried with SOQL; named credentials surface only through Apex callouts and merge fields.
probes.correct_answer: The NamedCredential object supports query(), so SOQL can read the record's endpoint and settings (the secret itself never comes back).

probes.question: If I raise sourceApiVersion to 63.0, will my existing Named Credentials be converted to the External Credential model automatically?
probes.wrong_answer: Yes. From API 56.0 the platform auto-migrates Named Credentials to the split External Credential + Named Credential model, so scripts written for the old fields break.
probes.correct_answer: No. Legacy remains a valid named credential type kept for backward compatibility; the External Credential model applies to credentials created as SecuredEndpoint, and raising the API version does not convert them.
